input.title: OKed approval review
input.prompt:
Run one pass of the OKed approval review loop.

Context: OKed sends approval cards for AI agent actions to Oren's Telegram and the OKed iPhone app. Some cards have the wrong risk tier (noise that causes approval fatigue, or risky steps marked safe), or weak text and layout. This task reviews the cards that reached Oren since the last run, fixes the classifier, card text and Telegram layout, records each change with its before and after, and ships when a hard gate passes.

Repos:
- oked-sdk: git checkout at ~/Dev/OKed (remote oked-ai/oked-sdk). The loop's tools and runbook live here.
- oked-app (backend, Telegram card renderer): ~/Dev/OKed/oked-app. Merging to its main deploys to Railway.
- oked-ios: ~/Dev/OKed/oked-ios. PRs only, never merge.
Never work in, switch branches in, or change those user checkouts. Make fresh git worktrees off origin/main in your scratchpad.

Steps:
1. In ~/Dev/OKed run `git fetch origin`. If `git show origin/main:docs/approval-review/RUNBOOK.md` fails, the loop is not merged yet: stop, do nothing, report "loop not installed yet".
2. Make a worktree of oked-sdk off origin/main in your scratchpad, on a branch named approval-review/<UTC time like 2026-10-19T0800>.
3. Read docs/approval-review/RUNBOOK.md in that worktree and follow it exactly, from step 0 to step 7. It holds the review rubric, the scripts to use (scripts/approval-review/*.mjs), the gate, the release, the record, and the notifications.
4. If `node scripts/approval-review/fetch.mjs` reports that GET /api/v1/history returns 404, the backend endpoint is not deployed yet: stop and report that.

Rules:
- Write all PR text, commit messages and record reasons in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Do not use em dashes.
- End commit messages with "Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>" and PR bodies with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)".
- Never change scripts/approval-review/, docs/approval-review/RUNBOOK.md, packages/claude-code or packages/receipt-core. Never create or change OKed rules. Never bypass or avoid an OKed approval card; it is the human check.
- Merge and release only when the gate prints "GATE: PASS". Otherwise leave the PR open and send one push notification with the gate reasons.
- Raw tool input from the history API can hold secrets. Keep it in the scratchpad. Only sanitized cases (via scripts/approval-review/corpus.mjs) go into the repo.
- Finish with a short report: cards reviewed, changes made (tier, text, layout), gate result, PR links, and the artifact page link from ~/.oked/review-state.json.
input.description: Every 4 hours: review recent OKed approval cards, fix tiers, text and layout, record before/after, ship when the gate passes.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='RELEASING.md'; s=open(p).read()
old='''### Why the workflow publishes one package per job'''
new='''### Adding a new package

npm only lets you attach a Trusted Publisher to a package that already exists, so the
**first** version of a new package (for example `@oked/receipt-core`, `@oked/verify`) is
published by hand from a maintainer's machine, before the tag that would publish it:

```bash
npm run build
cd packages/<name> && npm publish --access public
```

Then add the Trusted Publisher on npmjs (same fields as above) and list the package in the
`publish.yml` matrix. From the next tag on, CI publishes it like the others. A tag pushed
before the manual publish fails that package's job (`ENEEDAUTH`) while the rest publish.

### Why the workflow publishes one package per job'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
s=s.replace("A **Trusted Publisher** configured on npmjs for **each** of the 5 packages.","A **Trusted Publisher** configured on npmjs for **each** package.")
s=s.replace("All 5 use `oked-sdk`.","All of them use `oked-sdk`.")
s=s.replace("rewrites `version` in all 5 `packages/*/package.json` **and**","rewrites `version` in every `packages/*/package.json` **and**")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='.github/workflows/publish.yml'; s=open(p).read()
old='''          - openclaw-cli
'''
new='''          - openclaw-cli
          - receipt-core
'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cat > packages/receipt-core/README.md <<'EOF'
# @oked/receipt-core

The format and the cryptography of OKed signed approval receipts, shared by the
OKed backend (which signs), `@oked/sdk` (which verifies before an action runs)
and `@oked/verify` (which auditors run). One implementation, so all three
compute the same bytes and the same digests.

A receipt is a JSON body signed with Ed25519 over its RFC 8785 canonical form
(JCS). It proves who decided on an agent action, how they were verified, what
exact action they decided on, and when. See
[docs/receipts.md](https://github.com/oked-ai/oked-sdk/blob/main/docs/receipts.md)
for the format, what a receipt proves and what it does not.

```ts
import { verifyReceipt, verifyChain } from "@oked/receipt-core";

const keys = await (await fetch("https://api.oked.ai/.well-known/oked-receipt-keys.json")).json();
const check = verifyReceipt(receipt, { keys });
// { ok: true, problems: [] } or e.g. { ok: false, problems: ["bad_signature"] }
```

| Export | What it does |
|---|---|
| `canonicalize(value)` | RFC 8785 JCS. Throws on values JSON cannot carry. |
| `jsonValue(value)` | The value as the other side of a JSON request sees it (undefined becomes null). |
| `subjectDigest(subject)` | `sha256:` digest of what was authorized (`subject_core`). |
| `displayDigest(shown)` | `sha256:` digest of what the approver was shown. |
| `bodyDigest(body)` | A receipt body's digest; the next receipt's `prev_receipt_digest`. |
| `verifyReceipt(receipt, { keys, subject? })` | Shape, key window, signature and, given the original request, the subject digest. |
| `verifyChain(receipts, heads?)` | Seq gaps, broken `prev_receipt_digest` links, duplicates, and agreement with saved chain heads. |
| `signerFromSeed(seed, kid)`, `signBody(body, signer)` | Signing, for the issuer. |

Node 18+, ESM, no dependencies (uses `node:crypto`). MIT.
EOF
git diff --stat; git status --short
